implementationScope: package-only progressive JFIF 4:2:0 incremental session with semantic-unit transport, dynamic pre-SOF table ownership, SOF DQT ownership transfer, first-SOS DQT release, actual-only coefficient planes, exact current Huffman payloads, render-only quantization widening, packed four-bit progression state, live-strip fancy vertical boundary reconstruction and validated-EOI final-ready compaction

cases.mechanismPressure: single-strip control proves removing deferred-Y capacity changes only width-proportional render scratch while all ten previews and source semantics remain unchanged
36 iMCU rows repeatedly reconstruct row 15 from the still-live prior Y strip after new chroma is rendered; frozen v14 RGB SHA256 independently guards render-order correctness
four iMCU rows combine live-strip fancy boundary reconstruction with restart-heavy entropy suspension, proving render-order scratch removal is orthogonal to rollback

requiredInvariants: All v14 transport, dynamic table ownership, SOF DQT transfer, first-SOS release, source semantics, actual coefficient geometry, dynamic Huffman, render-only quantization widening, packed progression, restart, preview and EOI-compaction invariants remain unchanged.

For every qualified 4:2:0 render arena, rowStateBytes equals exactly 18*yRowStrideBytes + 18*chromaRowStrideBytes: 16 Y strip rows, 8 Cb rows, 8 Cr rows, prior Cb/Cr rows and reconstructed full-width Cb/Cr rows. No deferred Y row is allocated.

At an internal fancy vertical boundary, the next strip's chroma is rendered first; the previous strip's yStrip row 15 remains live and is combined with saved previous Cb/Cr row 7 plus current chroma row 0. Only after that boundary row is written may the next Y strip overwrite yStrip.

The 576x576 multi-iMCU source must retain the frozen v14 RGB SHA256 5b1738e18c84104586fbe59f37348d8bf1fd9af2cd7036874f156625549bafbb; incremental-versus-complete self-agreement is not sufficient evidence because both paths share the renderer.
Persistent state and maximum retained authority are unchanged from v14. Render scratch decreases by exactly one yRowStrideBytes per source: 64 bytes for tiny/restart64 and 576 bytes for noise576.
The tiny source has rowStateBytes 2304, renderScratchBytes 2816, totalStateBytes 6560, final-ready retained 897 bytes, maximum retained authority 5055 bytes and operation peak 7871 bytes.

The 576x576 source has rowStateBytes 16128, renderScratchBytes 16640, totalStateBytes 1014432, final-ready retained 995328 bytes, maximum retained authority 998206 bytes and operation peak 2010174 bytes.
The restart64 source has rowStateBytes 2304, renderScratchBytes 2816, totalStateBytes 17568, final-ready retained 12288 bytes, maximum retained authority 15166 bytes and operation peak 30270 bytes.

Pre-frame/frame-q/Huffman high-water, entropy rollback, source hashes and final RGB values remain identical to v14. This version removes only a render-order copy and does not widen the qualified source domain.

This profile does not qualify malloc headers, allocator size classes, Swift object/pointer fields, physical RSS, non-JFIF semantics, embedded ICC, other sampling modes or perceptual reconstruction quality.
